A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOKE research, despite the revised title and substantial extensions. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation and reconstruction experiments on How2Sign and CSL-Daily, an ASL user study, and pose-fitting results on SGNify in appendix Table S1.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments across three sign languages, decoding and retrieval ablations, ASL and CSL user evaluations, and retained SGNify pose-fitting results.

M1.justification: V1 generates body-part sequences through independent, weight-sharing decoders. V2 retains this as the parallel-decoding comparator and introduces multi-head decoding with shared, weighted part-token embeddings. It also adds dictionary retrieval, appending retrieved motion tokens to the encoder input. These substantially change generation and conditioning; the decoupled tokenizer and pose-fitting pipeline remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds Phoenix-2014T and German sign language to training and evaluation. MSASL, WLASL, SLR500, and DW-DGS supply new dictionary data for tokenizer training and retrieval. Human evaluation expands from ASL signers to ASL and CSL signers. How2Sign, CSL-Daily, and the appendix SGNify evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds an evaluated T2S-GPT baseline, which v1 only cites. Conversely, v1 Table 2's dedicated reconstruction comparisons against SignVAE and MotionVAE disappear. The other main generation comparators remain; MotionGPT is renamed S-MotionGPT, not introduced as a different baseline.

E3.justification: Reported per-GPU batches change from 256 to 320 for DETO and 24 to 32 for the LM. V2 adds latency testing on one RTX 3090, reports combined-hand and average DTW errors, drops ROUGE and tokenizer PA-MPVPE reporting, and evaluates tokenizer decompositions through generation errors. The user study adds four CSL judges to five ASL judges while retaining the stated rating scale and 15 generated examples per method.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled decoding/latency comparisons, quantitative and qualitative retrieval ablations, and sensitivity to embedding weight lambda. Multilingual scaling and tokenizer-decomposition analyses are substantially revised. V1's separate-face tokenizer configuration and start-token ablation disappear. Codebook-size sensitivity remains, with updated results and coverage.

E5.justification: Both versions report table point estimates and average user ratings with unexplained error bars in Figure 7. Neither specifies training seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The larger user study changes evaluation design, without introducing a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces SOKE results: How2Sign body DTW changes from 7.61 to 6.82 and BLEU-4 from 14.58 to 14.48; CSL-Daily BLEU-4 changes from 11.90 to 11.30. These accompany revised methods and training, rather than controlled version-to-version gains. German, retrieval, latency, and CSL user results are added, while tokenizer and ROUGE entries are removed. Appendix Table S1 is unchanged. V2 also has an unexplained Text2Mesh How2Sign row: Avg 11.94, Body 13.99, Hand 13.47.

T1.justification: V2 introduces the conditional-independence factorization for multi-head decoding in Equation 4 and its relationship to sequential decoding in Equation 2. The parallel factorization largely restates v1's procedure. This is a localized formal extension; tokenizer mathematics and appendix pose-fitting losses S1–S3 remain unchanged, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a novel decoupled tokenizer and unified generation across two sign languages. V2 treats decoupled tokenization as an existing foundation and foregrounds multi-head decoding's efficiency/fusion tradeoff and retrieval-enhanced precision. Dataset-curation and state-of-the-art claims expand to include Phoenix-2014T and three sign languages.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations that embedding averaging may reduce individual token errors, retrieved signs guide hand shapes, and shared cross-lingual signs contribute beyond additional training data. It also discusses avoiding unnatural transitions from directly concatenating dictionary signs. V1's explanation for unsuccessful separate-face modeling is removed. The limitation concerning unavoidable pseudo-pose reconstruction errors remains.

D1.justification: V2 documents dictionary construction, lemmatized lookup, Jieba segmentation, lowest-reconstruction-error exemplar selection, lambda settings, and decoding termination. It revises batch specifications but removes v1's split counts, three-block encoder specification, factor-four downsampling, and EMA-reset disclosure. A promise to release code, models, and data is added; the PDFs do not establish actual release.

R1.justification: Related work gains a substantial retrieval-generation discussion, including RAG, FLARE, ToG, and retrieval-based image generation. V2 explicitly situates decoupled tokenization relative to prior approaches, including HumanTOMATO, while reducing broader recognition/translation and standalone tokenizer coverage. Novelty is repositioned around decoding and retrieval, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around retrieval and multi-head decoding. The framework overview is condensed, methodology subsections are reorganized, and separate qualitative/quantitative evaluation sections become state-of-the-art comparison and ablation sections. Appendix organization also changes.

P2.justification: The overview is redrawn, a three-strategy decoding diagram and retrieval diagrams are introduced, and qualitative panels are reorganized across three languages. Tables gain new metric and dataset groupings, and Figure 7 becomes a grouped ASL/CSL chart. V1 Figure 3 moves to v2 Figure S4; reconstruction-comparison panels are removed rather than merely relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the paper through explicit tests of decoding quality versus latency, separate retrieval ablations, and human validation extending beyond ASL to CSL. Its positioning also more clearly distinguishes inherited tokenization from the proposed contributions. These provide stronger experimental and explanatory support than v1. Removed tokenizer/ROUGE evidence, reduced implementation disclosure, and the unexplained Text2Mesh row are drawbacks, but the controlled mechanism analyses and broader human validation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
